findings.issue: cw24 takes its kind list from the cw8 run (kinds). When the cw8 child is killed or answers nothing, kinds is empty, so cw24 goes red as well, with the text no second measurement for [] of []; got {}, which names no kind and hides that the cause is the cw8 child. A second red with a misleading text for one underlying fault.
findings.resolution: Fold the empty-kinds case into the message (for example: the cw8 child gave no kinds to compare), or read the kind names from asked itself and assert their set against the four expected labels. Optional, batch to the low list.

intent.note: Task clause: Let the job carry the step (job step, defaulting to WIDE_STEP) and add one permanent case that runs the child with the step at 0.5 and asserts the output holds an again entry with two seconds for every kind. Diff: the job gains step (cw8 job passes WIDE_STEP), last_step_again gains step=WIDE_STEP and the child passes job[step], and cw24 runs the child with a step and asserts an again entry of two positive seconds and no fault for every kind cw8 measured. One deviation from the letter, and an improvement: the asked step is 0.01 not 0.5. At 0.5 a last doubling could fall under it (a ratio of two sub-floor times, both read as the 1e-3 floor) and the case could flake; at 0.01 the ratio would need a reading about 90 times faster than measured here (0.47 ms at the shorter length of the fastest kind, 0.92 ms at the longer, over the 1e-3 floor in _last_step). Coarse clock (windows 1/64 s): growth_series keeps only batches whose total reached the floor (at least 10 clock steps and 0.02 s), so every per-call time is positive and about the same size at the two lengths; the clock step cannot push the ratio under 0.01 and the extra cost is a few seconds at most, so cw24 is not flaky on a slow or coarse-clock runner. The task premise that deleting the closure outright leaves cw8 green is partly wrong, and the executor says so: the name is evaluated eagerly, so removing the closure is red in cw8 too; the use, body, field, step and pair-length rows are the ones only cw24 sees, and the probe confirms it. The executor claim matches the diff: the _run_timer extraction keeps the kill and no-answer sentences, last_step_again keeps a default so the pure cases call it unchanged, and the cw24 label says what it asserts. Dependants: sweep-costs.json holds a whole-file figure only (the change adds about 0.7 s of the executor measured), _clause_coverage.py is untouched, CHANGELOG and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE name nothing changed; the answers hold. The floor guard could not compare the test file (code outside labelled checks changed); I read that code: the child job step and the helper signature are the only changes, no check weakened.
